NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24755  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH
AT GWALIOR
BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIRDESH  ON THE 6 th OF OCTOBER, 2025  MISC.
PETITION No. 7325 of 2023  THE NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA  Versus
AJAY BANSAL AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Ashish Saraswat - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Arun Dudawat and Shri Rahul Jha- Advocate for the  respondents.

ORDER The present misc. petition is preferred by petitioner- the National Highways Authority of India being aggrieved by order dated 18th of August, 2023 passed by Collector, District Gwalior in Case No.0209/B-121/2022- 2023, whereby the application preferred by respondent No.1 under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act has been allowed by passing an order of remand to the competent authority i.e. SDO (Land Acquisition), National Highway No.75, District Gwalior for re-adjudication.

It is the case of petitioner that as per Section 3(G)(6) of the Act, the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 are applicable in the matter pertaining to land acquisitions under the National Highways Act,1956.

As per Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, the Arbitrator could only determine the amount of compensation, either to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24755 2 MP-7325-2023 enhance the compensation amount or to reduce the compensation amount and the power of remand is not conferred on the Arbitrator.

The Arbitrator- cum-Collector was required to decide the case on the merits of the case and and he is not having power under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 to remand the matter to the competent authority i.e. SDO (Land Acquisition).
It is further contended that present matter is squarely covered by the judgment dated 11-10-2011 passed by Division Bench of this Court i n Sanjay

Section 3(G)(5) of the National High Courts Act, 1956 reads as under:-
'' If the amount determined by the competent authority under sub-section(1) or sub-section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties the amount shall on an application by either of the parties be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government.''

sentences.text:
Further sub-section (6) reads as under:-
''(6) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996( 26 of 1996) shall apply to every arbitration under this Act.''

A bare reading of sub-section (5) of Section 3G provides expressly that the Arbitrator,
appointed by Central Government which in the present case is the Collector, has to determine the amount.

After going through submissions of parties and above provisions as well as going through the judgment passed by Division Bench of this Court, this Court is of the considered opinion that the remand order passed by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24755 3 MP-7325-2023 Collector is not permissible in the teeth of the express word of Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act under which the Arbitrator could only determine the amount.

Because by the impugned order dated 18th of August, 2023 (Annexure P-1 to the misc. petition), the Collector, Gwalior while acting as Arbitrator, has not determined the amount but has remanded the matter, therefore, the instant misc. petition deserves to be and is hereby allowed.

The matter is remanded to the Collector, who shall re-examine and decide the matter in his capacity as Arbitrator within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
In view of aforesaid, this misc. petition stands disposed of.
